Definition: prolonged from a primary κάρ (Latin cor, "heart"); the heart, i.e. (figuratively) the thoughts or feelings (mind); also (by analogy) the middle:--(+ broken-)heart(-ed).
BiblicalUsage: Kardia is the heart — not only the muscle but the seat of thought, will, and love. The end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart; sanctify the Lord God in your hearts; if our heart condemn us, God is greater than our heart; and eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the heart is where everything is decided. God looks on the heart, the heart condemns or acquits, and the things He has prepared are beyond what the heart can even imagine — and that is why I ask Him to make mine pure and keep it His.
RelatedTopics: Human Nature; Purity; Love of God
